function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.content:
The title “greatest basketball player ever” is one of those classic debates that never really ends—different eras, different styles, and personal preferences all play a role. Here’s a quick snapshot of the most common contenders and why they’re often mentioned:

| Player | Era | Key Achievements | Why They’re Often Mentioned |
|--------|-----|------------------|-----------------------------|
| **Michael Jordan** | 1980s‑1990s | 6× NBA champion, 5× MVP, 14× All‑Star, 10× scoring champion | Dominated the NBA during the 1990s, unmatched clutch performances, global cultural impact |
| **LeBron James** | 2000s‑present | 4× NBA champion, 4× MVP, 19× All‑Star (as of 2024), 2× Olympic gold | Longevity, versatility (scoring, passing, rebounding), consistent excellence across multiple teams |
| **Kareem Abdul‑Jabbar** | 1970s‑1980s | 6× NBA champion, 6× MVP, 19× All‑Star, all‑time leading scorer | Record‑setting career points, dominant sky‑hook, longevity |
| **Bill Russell** | 1950s‑1960s | 11× NBA champion, 5× MVP, 12× All‑Star | Unmatched championship record, defensive dominance, leadership |
| **Magic Johnson** | 1980s | 5× NBA champion, 3× MVP, 12× All‑Star | Revolutionized the point‑guard position, flashy playmaking, 3‑point shooting pioneer |
| **Larry Bird** | 1980s | 3× NBA champion, 3× MVP, 12× All‑Star | Rivalry with Magic, clutch shooting, strong shooting guard/forward blend |

### Why the debate is so hard to settle

1. **Different Game Rules & Pace** – The NBA has evolved (e.g., shot clock changes, three‑point line introduction). Comparing stats across eras is tricky.
2. **Statistical vs. Intangible Impact** – Some players dominate the box score; others influence the game through leadership, defense, or cultural impact.
3. **Longevity vs. Peak Performance** – A player who dominates for a decade may be weighed against someone who had a shorter but more spectacular peak.

### Bottom Line

There isn’t a definitive answer. Many analysts and fans lean toward Michael Jordan for his combination of individual accolades, clutch moments, and cultural influence. Others argue that LeBron’s longevity and versatility make him the best overall. Kareem’s scoring record and Bill Russell’s championship legacy also keep them in the conversation. Ultimately, the “greatest” title depends on what you value most in a player—championships, individual skill, longevity, or cultural impact.
